Rashi on Chullin 7b:10:1.hebrew: מבתש - מפציר, וחברו בשבועות (דף ל:). מבתש גרסינן בבי"ת ולא בכ"ף:
Rashi on Chullin 7b:10:1.english: Mavatesh - [Meaning] pressing/urging insistently; its counterpart is in [tractate] Shevuot (page 30b). We read it as "mavatesh," with a bet, and not with a kaf.

Rashi on Chullin 7b:10:2.english: A mountain rose up between them - And it separated them.

Rashi on Chullin 7b:10:3.hebrew: בחייהן - של צדיקים, כך נותן הקדוש ברוך הוא לבו על תאותם שלא להעביר דעתם, שגרם הדבר שנכנס בפתח הפרדות שיפרוש ולא יעבור על דעתו הראשונה, שאין דרכו לסעוד משל אחרים, כדלקמן:
Rashi on Chullin 7b:10:3.english: In their lifetime - [Referring to] the righteous. Thus does the Holy One, Blessed be He, attend to their wishes, so as not to make them depart from their own resolve: He arranged matters so that when he came to the gateway where the mules were standing, it would cause him to turn back and not depart from his original resolve, since it was not his practice to dine on that which belonged to others, as [stated] below.

Rashi on Chullin 7b:10:4.hebrew: על אחת כמה וכמה - שהרי במיתתן גדולים יותר מבחייהן, כדאמר רבי חמא:
Rashi on Chullin 7b:10:4.english: All the more so - For [the righteous] are greater in their death than in their lifetime, as Rabbi Chama states.

Rashi on Chullin 7b:10:5.english: Burying a man - He was wicked, and therefore was not [fit] to be buried near the righteous.

Rashi on Chullin 7b:10:6.hebrew: ויגע האיש בעצמות אלישע ויחי - ואילו בחייו, כשרצה להחיות בן השונמית, הוצרך לשום פיו על פיו ועיניו על עיניו, ולבקש רחמים:
Rashi on Chullin 7b:10:6.english: And the man touched Elisha's bones, and he lived - Whereas during his [Elisha's] lifetime, when he wanted to revive the son of the Shunammite woman, he had to place his mouth on his mouth and his eyes on his eyes, and pray for mercy.

Rashi on Chullin 7b:11:1.hebrew: ודלמא לקיומי ברכתא דאליהו - דלא סגי שלא תתקיים, דכתיב בצדיקים (איוב כב) ותגזר אומר ויקם לך, ולאו משום אלישע הוה:
Rashi on Chullin 7b:11:1.english: And perhaps it was to fulfill Elijah's blessing - For it could not go unfulfilled, as it is written regarding the righteous (Job 22:28): "You will decree a matter, and it will be fulfilled for you." And it was not on account of Elisha.

Rashi on Chullin 7b:11:2.hebrew: פי שנים - אליהו החיה בן הצרפית, ואלישע בן השונמית, וצריך להחיות עוד אחר:
Rashi on Chullin 7b:11:2.english: A double portion - Elijah revived the son of the Tzarfite woman, and Elisha [revived] the son of the Shunammite woman; so [to have twice as many as Elijah,] he must revive yet another one.

Rashi on Chullin 7b:11:3.english: If so - [Meaning: if it is] in order to fulfill the blessing of Elijah.

Rashi on Chullin 7b:11:4.hebrew: היינו דתניא - בתמיה. ואי משום ברכתא דאליהו היה צריך להחיות ממש כמו שעשה אותו שהחיה אליהו, אלא לאו ש"מ משום אלישע הוה, ולא הוה צריך לאלישע אלא לסלקו מאצלו, והחייהו עד שנסתלק משם:
Rashi on Chullin 7b:11:4.english: Is this that which is taught in the baraita - [Abaye] said this as a question. And if it were on account of Elijah's blessing, he [Elisha] should have revived him fully, just as he [Elijah] did with the one whom Elijah revived. Rather, must one not conclude from this that it was on account of Elisha - and that the dead man did not actually need Elisha's power for anything but to be moved away from beside him, so he revived him only until he had moved away from there.

Rashi on Chullin 7b:12:1.english: Let her not, please, be like one dead - This is written regarding Miriam's leprosy.

Rashi on Chullin 7b:13:1.hebrew: למה נקרא שמם - דכודנייתא ימים, דכתיב (בראשית לו) אשר מצא את הימים:
Rashi on Chullin 7b:13:1.english: Why are they called by that name? - Because mules are called "yemim," as it is written (Genesis 36): "who found the yemim."

Rashi on Chullin 7b:13:2.hebrew: לא שאלני - רבי חנינא רופא היה, ומהכא מייתי לה במסכת יומא בהוציאו לו:
Rashi on Chullin 7b:13:2.english: He did not ask me - Rabbi Chanina was a doctor, and from here [the Gemara] derives this in Tractate Yoma, in the passage beginning "When they brought [the patient] out to him."

Rashi on Chullin 7b:13:3.english: And survived - This implies that the person who was struck [by the mule] would die [i.e., since Rabbi Ḥanina was never asked by a survivor, it must be that anyone struck by a white mule died].

Rashi on Chullin 7b:13:4.hebrew: וחיית - לשון נקבה, ואמכה קאי, שאין המכה מתרפאת:
Rashi on Chullin 7b:13:4.english: And it lived [ve-ḥayat] - This is [written in] the feminine form, referring to the wound [makkah], meaning that the wound does not heal.

Rashi on Chullin 7b:14:1.hebrew: אין עוד מלבדו - משום רבי חנינא נקט לה:
Rashi on Chullin 7b:14:1.english: "There is nothing else beside Him" - He cites this [verse] for the sake of [what he is about to say in the name of] Rabbi Chanina.

Rashi on Chullin 7b:14:2.hebrew: אפילו כשפים - אינן מלבדו, כלומר שלא מדעתו, שאם אין גזירה מלפניו אין מריעין לו לאדם:
Rashi on Chullin 7b:14:2.english: Even witchcraft - is not apart from Him, meaning it does not act without His will; for if there is no decree from before Him, it cannot harm a person.

Rashi on Chullin 7b:14:3.english: She goes around - She circles back and exerts herself so that he would not notice [what she was doing].

Rashi on Chullin 7b:14:4.english: To take dust - And to perform sorcery on him in order to kill him.

Rashi on Chullin 7b:14:5.hebrew: כשפים - נוטריקון מכחישים פמליא של מעלה, שלא גזרו על אדם זה למות והוא מת על ידי כשפים:
Rashi on Chullin 7b:14:5.english: Sorcery (keshafim) - This is an acronym for "they deny [the decree of] the heavenly entourage" (מכחישים פמליא של מעלה) - meaning that it was not decreed for this person to die, yet he dies by sorcery.

Rashi on Chullin 7b:15:1.english: Nokef (knocks) - [Means] strikes; in Old French, "eschopier" [to stub/knock].

Rashi on Chullin 7b:15:2.english: They proclaim [a ban] concerning him - They decreed against him.

Rashi on Chullin 7b:15:4.english: The right thumb - Because it strikes with force and suffers great pain.

Rashi on Chullin 7b:15:5.english: And on a second knock - Before the first has healed.

Rashi on Chullin 7b:16:1.hebrew: בצע - ברכת המוציא, שלא רצה לאכול כזית משל אחרים:
Rashi on Chullin 7b:16:1.english: He cut [the bread] - [This refers to] the blessing of Hamotzi: he did not want to eat an olive's-bulk [of bread] belonging to others.

Rashi on Chullin 7b:1:1.hebrew: חבטינהו - בנפה חבטינהו לנקותם, וויניר"א בלע"ז. וליכא למימר לשון דישה, דמעיקרא היו עומדים בקליפתן, דאם כן אמאי לא אכלה מעיקרא, הרי לא נתחייבו במעשר עד שיתמרחו בכרי, דכתיב ראשית דגנך, ותנן בהדיא (פאה פ"א מ"ו) מאכיל לבהמה לחיה ולעופות עד אשר ימרח, דכל אכילת בהמה חשיב אכילת עראי:
Rashi on Chullin 7b:1:1.english: He beat them - He beat them in a sieve to clean them; "vanner" [to winnow] in Old French. And one cannot say this is a term for threshing, [meaning] that beforehand they stood in their husks, for if so, why did she [the donkey] not eat it beforehand? Since they had not yet become obligated in tithes until they were smoothed out in the pile, as it is written, "the first of your grain," and we learned explicitly (Peah 1:6): One feeds animals, wild beasts, and fowl [with untithed produce] until it is smoothed out, for all eating by animals is considered casual eating.

Rashi on Chullin 7b:1:2.english: Pick them out - By hand, from among the stones and the refuse.

Rashi on Chullin 7b:2:1.hebrew: ומי מיחייבא - מאכל בהמה הנלקח מעם הארץ, כלום גזרו עליו משום דמאי? ואע"פ שאילו ודאי לא עישרו היה מחייב לעשר, על ספק מיהא לא גזור. דתנן: הלוקח מעם הארץ פירות מן השוק לזרע ולבהמה, אע"פ שהזרע ומאכל בהמה בכלל שאר תבואה הן וחייבין במעשרות, לא גזרו עליהם משום דמאי, דמסתמא רוב עמי הארץ מעשרין הן, ולא החמירו חכמים על הדמאי כל כך:
Rashi on Chullin 7b:2:1.english: But is it obligated? - Animal feed purchased from an am ha'aretz (a person not trusted regarding tithes) - did [the Sages] decree demai status upon it at all? And although if it were definitely untithed one would be obligated to tithe it, in a case of mere doubt they did not decree [demai]. As we learned [in a mishnah]: One who buys produce from an am ha'aretz in the market for seed or for animal feed - even though seed and animal feed are included among the rest of the produce and are obligated in tithes - [the Sages] did not decree demai status upon them, since presumably most amei ha'aretz do tithe, and the Sages were not so stringent about demai.

Rashi on Chullin 7b:3:1.english: But it was taught in a baraita - [To be read] as a statement [not a question]. And these measures, a person adopted them from the outset.

Rashi on Chullin 7b:4:1.english: Rabbi heard - That Rabbi Pinchas [ben Yair] was coming.

Rashi on Chullin 7b:4:2.hebrew: רצונך סעוד אצלי - יהי רצונך לסעוד אצלי:
Rashi on Chullin 7b:4:2.english: Would you like to dine with me - [Meaning:] May it be your will to dine with me.

Rashi on Chullin 7b:4:3.hebrew: צהבו פניו - שמח מפני שלא היה ר' פינחס רגיל ליהנות משל אחרים, כדלקמן:
Rashi on Chullin 7b:4:3.english: His face brightened - He was glad, because R. Pinchas was not accustomed to benefit from what belonged to others, as [will be explained] below.

Rashi on Chullin 7b:5:1.hebrew: אמר ליה - רבי פינחס, וכי סבור היית שמודר הנאה מישראל אני:
Rashi on Chullin 7b:5:1.english: He said to him - [i.e.,] Rabbi Pinchas [said to him]: Did you actually think that I forgo benefit from a fellow Jew?

Rashi on Chullin 7b:5:2.hebrew: ישראל קדושים הם - וראויין ליהנות מהם:
Rashi on Chullin 7b:5:2.english: The Jewish people are holy - And are fit to benefit from them.

Rashi on Chullin 7b:5:3.hebrew: אבל יש רוצה - לההנות אחרים משלו, ואין יכולת בידו, וממנו איני רוצה ליהנות, שלא אכביד עליו:
Rashi on Chullin 7b:5:3.english: But there is one who wants - To give benefit to others from what is his, but lacks the means to do so; and from him I do not want to derive benefit, so that I not burden him.

Rashi on Chullin 7b:5:4.hebrew: ויש שיש - יכולת בידו, ואינו רוצה לההנות אחרים, ואע"פ שאומר בא וסעוד אין לבו חפץ, ואיני נהנה ממנו, משום דכתיב אל תלחם לחם רע עין:
Rashi on Chullin 7b:5:4.english: And there is one who has - the means, but does not want to let others benefit from it. And although he says, "Come and dine," his heart does not desire it, and [therefore] I do not wish to benefit from him, since it is written, "Do not eat the bread of a stingy [lit. evil-eyed] person" (Proverbs 23:6).

Rashi on Chullin 7b:5:5.english: Do not eat bread - Do not dine. "Bread" is a term for a meal, as it is written (I Samuel 20): "he did not come to the meal," and as it is written (Daniel 5): "Belshazzar the king made a great feast."

Rashi on Chullin 7b:5:6.english: Like a gate - As if you are opening a gate in his stomach. And some say it is an expression of bitterness, as in (Jeremiah 29) "like wretched figs" (כתאנים השוערים).

Rashi on Chullin 7b:6:1.hebrew: מסרהיבנא - לשון בהלה ומהירות, כלומר צריך למהר ולילך לדבר מצוה ואין פנאי לסעוד:
Rashi on Chullin 7b:6:1.english: Masrhivna (I am rushing) - An expression of haste and speed, meaning that he needs to hurry and go off to perform a mitzvah, and there is no time to dine.

Rashi on Chullin 7b:7:1.english: Kudanyata (mules) - [These were] mules, and they belonged to Rabbi.

Rashi on Chullin 7b:7:2.english: The Angel of Death - Who strikes, and the one who is struck never lives again, as [will be explained] further on.

Rashi on Chullin 7b:8:1.hebrew: ולפני עור וגו' - דכי היכי דאסירן לך אסירן לאחריני. והא ליכא למימר דמזבן להו לעובדי כוכבים, דתנן אין מוכרין להם בהמה גסה (ע"ז דף יד:):
Rashi on Chullin 7b:8:1.english: And before a blind person, etc. - For just as they are forbidden to you, they are forbidden to others. And one cannot say that he will sell them to idolaters [instead], for we learned [in a mishna]: One may not sell them large livestock (Avodah Zarah, page 14b).

Rashi on Chullin 7b:9:1.hebrew: מפקרנא להו - אשלחם ביערות דעלמא להפקר:
Rashi on Chullin 7b:9:1.english: I will render them ownerless - I will send them off to the forests of the world to be ownerless.

Rashi on Chullin 7b:9:2.english: Because the damage would spread - Since they would no longer be guarded, their damage will increase.

Rashi on Chullin 7b:9:3.hebrew: עקרנא - שלא יוכלו לבעט, ובל תשחית ליכא, שיהו ראויות לדישה:
Rashi on Chullin 7b:9:3.english: I will hamstring them - So that they will not be able to kick, and there is no violation of "do not destroy" [bal tashchit], since they will still be fit for threshing.

Rashi on Chullin 7b:9:4.english: I will hamstring them - He saws through their hooves, and they are still able to walk.

Tosafot on Chullin 7b:10:1.hebrew: גדולים צדיקים במיתתן יותר מבחייהם כו' - פירש בקונטרס דדריש ממה שהחיה בנגיעה בעלמא, כדכתיב ויגע ויחי. וקשה דא"כ מאי פריך ודילמא לקיומי ברכתא דאליהו, מ"מ היה גדול במה שטרח להחיותו בחייו יותר מבמותו. ונראה דנפקא ליה ממה שבחיי הצדיקים נוגעים בהם כמה רשעים ויושבים אצלם, ושם לא היה לו רשות להתעכב אצלו:
Tosafot on Chullin 7b:10:1.english: Greater are the righteous in their death than in their lives, etc. - Rashi explained that this is derived from the fact that he revived [the dead man] through mere contact, as it is written, "and he touched, and he lived." And this is difficult: if so, what does [the Gemara] ask, "but perhaps [it was] to fulfill the blessing of Eliyahu"? In any case, he was greater in that he exerted himself to revive [the child] in his lifetime more than in his death. And it appears that he derives it from the fact that during the lifetime of the righteous, many wicked people touch them and sit beside them; but there, [he] had no license to tarry with him.

Tosafot on Chullin 7b:3:1.hebrew: הא אתמר עלה אמר רבי יוחנן כו' - במסכת שקלים (פ"ה ה"א) ובמסכת דמאי בירושלמי ובבראשית רבה (פ' ס'), לא משני מידי, אלא השיב להם דמחמרא אנפשה:
Tosafot on Chullin 7b:3:1.english: Was it not stated regarding this, Rabbi Yochanan said, etc. - In Tractate Shekalim (5:1), and in Tractate Demai in the Yerushalmi, and in Bereishit Rabbah (ch. 60), it does not resolve the matter at all; rather, it answered them that she was stringent with herself.

Tosafot on Chullin 7b:5:1.hebrew: ויש שיש לו ואינו רוצה - ואפ"ה איקרו קדושים, שמזמן את חבירו לאכול אצלו מפני הבושת:
Tosafot on Chullin 7b:5:1.english: And there is one who has [the means] but does not want [to invite others] - Even so, they are called "holy ones" - [referring to] one who invites his fellow to eat at his place because of the shame [of not doing so].

Tosafot on Chullin 7b:6:1.hebrew: מסרהבנא - ממהר אני, כדמתרגמינן וימהרו לשפוך דם (משלי א) ויסרהבון:
Tosafot on Chullin 7b:6:1.english: I am hurrying - I am hastening, as we translate "and they hasten to shed blood" (Proverbs 1:16) as "ve-yisrahavun" (ויסרהבון).
